features.description: optional: the one feature set every seat's launch pins, as name=true or name=false; each pair rides the launch as a trailing -c features.<pair>, so the CLI's last-wins config rule makes it the seat's effective value

oneOf.description: A first-message CLI whose launch line takes an initial prompt: the line that points at the seat's rules file rides the launch, never typed. `positional` is a bare trailing prompt; any other value is the option before it.

delivery.description: the measured way an idle seat of this CLI is reached: an event adapter that wakes it (channel, cross-session socket), its own runtime queue between turns, an MCP inbox read on a turn, or nothing; the launch refines it (src/launch/delivery-class.ts)

standing_rules.description: optional: rules the profile carries for every seat of this CLI, over the team file's; they ride with the file's rules in every delivery

herdr_status.description: optional: whether herdr reports this CLI's agent status faithfully; with unreliable, a screen the profile reads idle counts as free whatever herdr says

exit.description: what is typed into an idle prompt to make the CLI exit; a profile carries this or exit_keys, never both

exit_keys.description: the keys that exit the CLI from its idle screen, in order, for a CLI that takes no exit text; a profile carries this or exit, never both

session_cli.description: optional: the CLI's own session-creating and session-pulling calls, as a run measured them — the whole body rides the creating call as one argument; absent, its seats have no session leg

argv.description: the binary and its own subcommand words; the task argument follows them

repo_flag.description: the option a repository is passed as, before the task; absent when the CLI takes none and chooses from its working folder

created.description: the line prefix the CLI prints once a session exists; the session id follows it

pull.description: the binary and its own subcommand words for pulling one session's result; --session <id> --apply follow them

public_only.description: optional: whether every seat of this CLI is public-only — the team's rules are never prepended to its briefs, and a send scans the whole body against the machine's private lists before the CLI's session call, refusing a body that matches one; absent reads as false, and a hosted CLI whose sessions run on another service sets true

exit_clear.description: optional: the one key that empties the CLI's input box, sent only to clear an exit text that did not read back as typed; absent, the text is left for the owner

exit_confirm.description: optional: the one key that confirms the CLI's own exit question, sent by a stop on a screen the profile reads as an exit question; absent, a seat that asks the question cannot be stopped by asking

exit_completion.description: optional: the CLI draws its own completion row for the exit text inside the box, so an Enter pressed before the row settles is drawn as a typed newline instead of running the command; the composer declares that row in own_rows. True: the exit typing waits the measured settle after the box reads back, presses Enter once more on the text-plus-one-empty-row frame an early Enter leaves, and clears an exit text the CLI never ran with exit_clear. Absent (false) where no capture shows a completion row.

input.description: optional: the measured way into this CLI's input box — its clear keys and paste surface; absent, a delivery that finds unsent text holds it untouched, and a restart refuses

clear.description: the keys that empty the box on an idle screen, sent in order and repeated until the box reads empty

clear_working.description: the keys that empty the box during a running turn, measured on a CLI that takes text there

paste.description: how text is put back into the box: bracketed paste

mid_turn.description: whether this CLI takes text into its box while a turn runs; true requires clear_working, and false leaves a draft found on a working screen held

lobby_files.description: optional: the exact relative paths of regular files a capture showed this CLI writing in its working folder; absent, this CLI is not recorded as writing a file there

startup_reads.description: optional: paths this CLI reads at start in its working folder; a trailing slash names a directory and every file under it, and the lobby gate refuses each of these at any depth

not_started.description: optional: startup screens drawn before the CLI started a session; team down closes such a pane without typing, never choosing an option

abandon_answers.description: optional: prompts team down --abandon answers so the seat closes fully; keys are only escape, ctrl+c or ctrl+u, never a menu option

typed_wake.description: optional: the one wake a send may type into this CLI's pane; screen types one trigger line into an empty idle box seen on two reads and calls the send delivered only when the profile's working screen shows; absent, the typed leg never runs for this CLI

read_hint.description: optional: the one sentence a typed wake appends after the message's header so the seat takes its fastest read path; absent, the shipped 'Read it with: team drops --read.'

watch_wake.description: optional: whether the watch's unread pass may type the same wake a send types when a message has gone unread past its window; on by default exactly where typed_wake is declared, and it cannot be turned on without one

watch_wake_tries.description: optional: how many typed wake attempts one message gets from the watch's unread pass, the first at the window and each later after a backoff; default 3; refused unless watch_wake is on

mcp_inbox.description: optional: the team inbox's measured registration for this CLI; absent, its seats stay on the drop and typed legs

launch_args.description: arguments appended to the launch line; {seat}, {session}, {command} and {entry} are filled from the launch; {command_json}, {entry_json} and {seat_json} are the same values escaped for a double-quoted string inside a structured word; {file_args} is the server's --file pair as array elements when the launch named the team file, nothing otherwise

add.description: the CLI's own mcp add subcommand arguments, run in the seat's folder at launch; {inbox}, {seat}, {session}, {command} and {entry} are filled from the launch, and a whole {file} word is the launch's --file pair when it names the team file, nothing otherwise; with a target the add writes that project file, without one it writes the CLI's own user-level store

target.description: the file add writes inside the seat's folder, relative to it; absent, the add writes the CLI's own user-level store

file.description: a config file team writes itself, relative to the seat's folder

remove.description: the CLI's own command that removes this seat's user-level entry, run by team down and team remove for a seat they close; {inbox} is the entry name, team-inbox-<session>-<seat>-<hash>; it needs add and no target

settings.description: optional: a session-settings option the launch carries; {cwd} in the value is the seat's absolute launch folder, escaped as the inside of a JSON string

vendors.description: optional: the vendors this CLI can run for with no launcher script — each vendor's env words ({credential} and {model} fill them), the credential item this machine must hold, and the model ids it offers; declared together with credentials

credential.description: the item this machine's credential store must hold before a seat may move to this vendor

env.description: the shell words the launch line sets before the CLI: each sets one variable, and {model} is the model id and {credential} the item

credentials.description: optional: how this machine's store is asked whether it holds a vendor's item — the attribute-only lookup, the one-time add command a refusal prints, and the status the store answers for an absent item; declared together with vendors

check.description: the lookup, without the secret: nothing here asks for the item's value

add.description: the one-time command that adds a missing item; {item} is its name, and the command asks the store for the secret itself

missing_status.description: the exit status that means the store holds no such item

status_model.description: optional: absent, the CLI's screen doesn't show its model

last_used_model.description: optional: the CLI starts on its last-used model when a launch names none

unread_model.description: optional: launch names no model read from the screen but the launch line's own, labelled (from launch)

kind.description: The dialog kind this record answers.

key.description: The key the profile presses: one that dismisses the dialog, never one that picks a menu option.

to.description: Equal to from for one exact version, matched byte for byte; otherwise a closed range of whole versions.

capture.description: The registered capture this record's predicate, label and extractor were taken from: the manifest's whole path, not a basename.

lobby_evidence.description: Codex only: a registered capture of the folder-only layout taken in the real lobby. Other CLIs must not claim it.

join.description: Join the rows after the anchor only when they prove one wrapped path: the first fills the wrap column, each later row starts at the indent. Off, the extractor refuses a run with more than one row.

indent.description: With join: the continuation column the capture draws.

wrap.description: With join: the column the capture's first wrapped row fills exactly.

turn_end.description: optional: the row that ends a turn — the CLI's own completion line. A `live` rule's region is the newest turn above the composer, and a turn-end row closes the turn it ends: every transcript row above the last one is a turn the pane has already scrolled past, so an error a completion ended is history while an error after the completion is still current. The pattern must match the whole row: "^…$". Absent: the whole paragraph above the composer is the newest turn.

plan_approval.description: A plan the agent wrote and waits to execute, drawn with the same numbered choice a permission dialog uses: read before permission.

confirmation.description: A confirmation the CLI or the agent raises before acting: read before permission for the same reason.

login.description: The CLI's own login screen: read after permission so a shipped permission pattern keeps the reading it had, and never answered.

footer.description: The first reported layout: the CLI's scroll-back footer as the whole row it draws, "^…$", on the pane's last non-blank row with the composer hidden. Read only where the composer cannot be read, after every caution stage.

marker.description: The second reported layout: the whole row of the CLI's return marker, "^…$", as the nearest non-blank row above the drawn composer. Read only together with "status_footer", where the composer cannot be read.

status_footer.description: The whole row of the CLI's scroll-back status footer, "^…$", on the pane's last non-blank row beneath the marker and the drawn composer. Read only together with "marker".

return_key.description: The key the CLI's own row names for returning to the prompt. Only a key a run established at this screen.

prompt.description: The CLI's feedback survey prompt row as the whole row it draws, "^…$", immediately above "choices" at the bottom of the pane.

choices.description: The CLI's feedback survey choices row as the whole row it draws, "^…$", immediately below "prompt" at the bottom of the pane.

status_footer.description: Optional whole-row pattern, "^…$", for the CLI's own status/shortcuts footer row when it remains drawn on the last non-blank row beneath the two survey rows.

skip_key.description: The key the survey's own Skip option names ('0'). Only '0' is permitted, and it is sent at most once before re-reading for an empty idle prompt.

any.description: The place every dialog kind takes when it has no entry of its own.

inline.description: The matched row is the question text.

after.description: The rows below the matched row are the question text.

before.description: The rows above the matched row are the question text.

until.description: The row that ends the block — the dialog's options or its footer, tested against the raw row. A block still going when `rows` runs out is reported cut rather than read part-way.

rows.description: How many consecutive rows may be taken; the walk stops at the first row that is blank after the strips.

strip.description: Patterns removed from each taken row before it is trimmed: a box border, the CLI's counter, the option number.

ignore_case.description: Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds (a long s or a Kelvin sign reads as itself). The flag reaches every rule of the stage, the exceptions written beside a match included.

reason.description: Optional rate-limit action reason carried into blocked status and watch reports.

vendorNotice.description: A vendor's own notice — an update screen, for one. Never answered, and never a reading without a record: the `tested` range is the version the capture was taken on, and the loader requires it. The list form is refused.

ignore_case.description: Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds. The flag reaches every rule of the stage, the exceptions written beside a match included.

rule.description: A rule matches on one of these primitives: any, all, footer, below_last_rule, none_after, only_after, block, or without_rule: true. on_footer, live and at_composer narrow a match one of them makes, and reason labels a rate-limit match; none of them matches alone.

reason.description: Optional action reason carried into blocked status and watch reports when this rate-limit rule matches.

live.description: an any/all rule read on the live region alone: the composer's own rows and the newest turn above them, never a turn the window has scrolled past

at_composer.description: an any/all rule read on the block of rows directly above the composer alone: blanks are skipped, every non-blank row of the block must match the rule, and the block ends at the first row that does not (or at the profile's turn_end). A composer that cannot be read leaves the whole window to the rule, so a wall already held stays held

ruleWithoutReason.description: A rule outside a rate-limit stage: `reason` labels a rate-limit match alone, so the loader refuses it on any other stage's rule as an unknown key.

ignore_case.description: Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds (a long s or a Kelvin sign reads as itself). The flag is the entry's, so it reaches the except list beside the match.
Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds (a long s or a Kelvin sign reads as itself).

flag.description: The model id to suggest for this model and version. "{version}" is the seat's version.

ignore_case.description: Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds (a long s or a Kelvin sign reads as itself).

flag.description: The model id to suggest for this model and version. "{version}" is the seat's version.

yields.description: The exact model names this rule's templates spell, as the reader reads them back — a closed list, never a pattern, each name once. Absent or empty: the rule yields no model (a template that cannot fill, like an id a launch line shows but the screen never does).

version_like.description: The version shapes this rule can spell its models with: a regular expression source anchored at both ends ("^" and "$"), tested against the whole version. Absent: the rule spells no version. A source not anchored at both ends is refused as the profile loads.

absent.description: What a launch that names no model does. last-used: the CLI starts on whatever model it used last.

status_line.description: The status line's patterns: one string, or a list where one pattern per family would not fit the dialect's length cap. A line is a candidate when it matches any entry.

status_below.description: Where the status row must sit, declared only for a CLI whose captures show the pane drawing a workspace line under it. The line directly under the row must match `line` and be the pane's last non-blank one, and the `  →` input row must sit above the row within the distance the captures show; a grammar line anywhere else is ordinary text. A row matching `except` keeps its grammar-only reading, wherever it is — the reading it had before this field existed. A bare string is `line` with no exemption.

status.description: A box composer's status row, under its closing rule: the same shape `status_line` takes, read only for box-to-rule and only under the rule. Only a CLI whose capture shows a figure there declares it (grok's footer).

ignore_case.description: Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds (a long s or a Kelvin sign reads as itself). Only two-rules-footer-below reads it; a composer's other modes refuse the key at load.

placeholder_fg.description: The foregrounds a CLI draws its rotating hints in, as SGR parameter lists (`90`, `38;5;244`, `38;2;103;108;116`), measured off a capture. An input row whose visible text past the prompt is exactly one of these colours is the empty box, with no faint attribute needed (Muse 1.4.14's rotating hint). Only a measured colour is declared — an undeclared one keeps the row text. Requires placeholder_style: dim.

wrap.description: How the composer continues a line onto its next row, declared only where a capture showed the wrap. The box is compared with the typed text under this rule: only the whitespace the row break itself stands for is normalised, the rest of every row must match character for character.

own_rows.description: Rows the pane draws of its own inside the composer's box — between the input row and the status row, or between the input row and the closing rule — declared only where a capture shows them (Muse's completion row for the text being typed). A matching row is not text in the box. status-then-one and box-to-rule read the key.

chrome.description: The pane's own chrome row under the status line: one string, or a list read as the union, each matching the whole line. Only status-then-one reads the key. Declared, a line under the status row is chrome only when it matches — any other line there leaves the row unread, so text the seat prints can never stand in for the pane's row and feed a quota figure. A composer that declares none keeps the trailing rule it had.

frame_rows.description: The empty rows a capture shows the pane drawing under the text, inside the box's frame (the drop before the status line or the closing rule). The box read strips up to this many trailing empty rows as the frame; a row beyond them is one the typed text does not have, and the box is refused. Zero where no capture shows such a row: don't guess.

border.description: The box's own border rows, declared only for a CLI whose captures draw them: `top` the row directly above the input row, `bottom` the row directly below the input rows and directly above the status row, both whole rows at one width (the captures draw them at the pane's width). The bordered frame is read beside the blank one; a frame with only one of the two rows, a row displaced from the input row or the status row, or a border-shaped row inside the box leaves the screen unknown. A composer without this field reads only the blank frame.
